title: Loading feedback proportional to wait and task
summary: Communicate progress in a way proportional to the expected wait, preserving known content when possible and distinguishing loading from failure.
problem: A generic spinner hides whether work started, what remains usable, and whether the system is stuck.
use_when: An operation takes long enough for the user to notice
Data or processing may arrive incrementally
avoid_when: The operation completes effectively instantly and feedback would create flicker
rationale: Users need acknowledgement first, then progress detail as waits grow.
Retaining existing content reduces layout shifts and cognitive disruption.

use_if: An operation takes long enough for the user to notice
Data or processing may arrive incrementally
prefer_alternatives_if: The operation is instant or can be handled optimistically without ambiguity

requirements: Expose meaningful busy or status state without trapping focus.
Avoid indefinite motion as the only signal.
reduced_motion: Use nonessential animation only when allowed by user or platform preference.

requirements: Prefer skeleton or content preservation only when it reflects real layout, not decorative shimmer.
Use determinate progress when reliable progress is known.
